title: Harry's band and its substitutes
summary: Joe lists Harry's band and who filled in for Harold: Tat (Adolf Alexander), Handy and Jesse Charles.

story.theme_name: Who was in the band: naming sidemen and personnel
story.community_name: Who played in the band: reciting personnel

blocks.x: Well anyhow, that was the first, not the first, but that was the last thing. We worked out there, and that's the last time I worked with Buddy. And as the calendar clicks off as it does, Harry, I put it there, we organized, not we, he did, and he got me to work on it with him. We worked here in the Bay, and Claremont Harbour, and the Kill, and the Ditto, and so forth and on. And we got along and we were fine. Well that band consists of Harry Fanky, who, as he told you, he had picked up his trumpet hand. It was myself on the piano, his brother-in-law Chip on the guitar, Eddie Thomas on the drum. Let's see, was anyone else out there? Kind of hard to think of. Harold. Yeah, Harold on his saxophone. Right. Man, look at that.

And by me being in New Orleans, every day, I could contact Harold, mostly any time I want, I used to catch him by the Whitney Bank. By the Whitney Bank, yeah. Yeah, because I used to carry a railroad mail there all the time. That's right. Yeah. So we worked together for many, many years, I'll put it to that. And, uh, yeah. And when Harold couldn't come, that's how Tat came into the picture. Yeah, I said Tat. He sent Tat once or twice. Who's Tat? Adolf Alexander. Are you trying to think of his name? Adolf Alexander's Tat.

Yeah. Yeah, that's his name. He sent Tat a couple of times, and once before Clash Hall came. Yeah. Remember? Yeah. And I don't know what happened along the line, sometime, uh, another, Harold was busy, something, and Handy got into the picture.
Well, I sent Handy when I was on a regular job.
Yeah. So by Handy being, living out here all the weekends, and you was on a regular job, we had once or twice.
Yeah, so then Handy got in. And then Handy said, Jesse Charles.
